title: the WSG rope - using rope for movement and climbing
audit_label: R440 WSG rope use pin audit
audit_comment: The rope-use slice pins the standard 50-foot coil (the most important climbing equipment), the 1500-pound support limit, the 20 percent per-turn non-cumulative overload break chance, the cumulative 10/30/60/100 weakening ladder and the 40 percent weakened-rope break chance (rules/wsgrope.h, prefix wsr); census 364 -> 365.

banner.title: The WSG USING ROPE FOR MOVEMENT AND CLIMBING, R440: the rope prose (no table this round) - characters are not expected to climb slopes or cliff faces relying only on the strength and dexterity of their hands and feet; certain equipment is available and often necessary for a severe slope or a cliff face, and the single most important equipment any climber can have is a coil of rope. The standard 50-foot coil is assumed somewhat smaller than half an inch in diameter and supports up to 1500 pounds without danger of fraying or breaking; if the limit is exceeded there is a 20 percent chance per turn (non-cumulative, while the strain remains) that it breaks; if it does not break, the cumulative chance it has become weakened from the stress is 10 percent after one turn, 30 after two, 60 after three and 100 after four; a weakened rope breaks the next time it supports more than its limit at 40 percent per turn (non-cumulative) - the round continues the movement-across-special-terrain section. Census 364 -> 365.
banner.provenance: the WSG scan (archive.org item pdfy-B3Fz83tZ3TV7zOc8), printed p. 36; the user own copy OCR cross-checked against the archive djvu word layer - the section reads CLEAN in the djvu, every number (the 50-foot coil, the 1500 pounds, the 20 percent, the 10/30/60/100 ladder and the 40 percent) matched exactly; no eye-reads were needed.
banner.sentinel: The standard 50-foot coil supports up to 1500 pounds without danger of fraying or breaking. Past the limit the break chance is 20 percent per turn non-cumulative; the weakening chance is cumulative - 10/30/60/100 percent by the turn of strain - and a weakened rope breaks at 40 percent per turn non-cumulative.

consts.name: wsrCoilLengthFt
consts.comment: The standard coil of rope is 50 feet long - the single most important equipment any climber can have.

consts.name: wsrMaxLoadLbs
consts.comment: A rope of the standard diameter can support up to 1500 pounds without being in danger of fraying or breaking.

consts.name: wsrOverloadBreakPct
consts.comment: If the weight limit is exceeded, there is a 20 percent chance per turn (non-cumulative), while the strain remains on the rope, that it will break.

consts.name: wsrWeakenedBreakPct
consts.comment: The chance of a weakened rope breaking the next time it is used to support more than its weight limit is 40 percent per turn (non-cumulative).

bools.name: wsrNotHandsAndFeetAlone
bools.comment: Characters are not expected to climb slopes or cliff faces while relying only on the strength and dexterity of their hands and feet.

bools.name: wsrEquipmentOftenNecessary
bools.comment: Certain equipment is available (and often necessary) to assist a character in climbing a severe slope or a cliff face.

bools.name: wsrRopeMostImportant
bools.comment: The single most important equipment any climber can have is a coil of rope.

bools.name: wsrCoilUnderHalfInch
bools.comment: The standard 50-foot coil of rope is assumed to be somewhat smaller than half an inch in diameter.

bools.name: wsrOverloadBreakNonCumulative
bools.comment: The overload break chance is per turn and non-cumulative, applying while the strain remains on the rope.

bools.name: wsrWeakenCumulativePerTurn
bools.comment: If the overloaded rope does not break, there is a 10 percent chance, cumulative per turn, that it has become weakened from the stress.

bools.name: wsrWeakenedBreakNonCumulative
bools.comment: The weakened-rope break chance is per turn and non-cumulative, applying the next time the rope is used to support more than its weight limit.

switches.name: wsrWeakenPct
switches.comment: The cumulative chance a rope strained past its weight limit has become weakened, by turns of strain: 0 at the start, 10 percent after one turn, 30 after two, 60 after three, 100 after four - and it stays 100 beyond that.

examples.note: the standard coil: 50 feet of rope supporting up to 1500 pounds without fraying or breaking

examples.expr: m['wsrWeakenPct'](1) != 10 or m['wsrWeakenPct'](2) != 30 or m['wsrWeakenPct'](3) != 60 or m['wsrWeakenPct'](4) != 100
examples.note: the cumulative weakening ladder: 10 percent after one turn of strain, 30 after two, 60 after three, 100 after four
the two break chances: the weakened rope breaks at 40 percent per turn - twice the 20 percent overload break chance of a healthy rope

table_checks.expr: m['wsrWeakenPct'](0) >= m['wsrWeakenPct'](1) or m['wsrWeakenPct'](1) >= m['wsrWeakenPct'](2) or m['wsrWeakenPct'](2) >= m['wsrWeakenPct'](3) or m['wsrWeakenPct'](3) >= m['wsrWeakenPct'](4)
table_checks.note: the weakening ladder is strictly increasing turn by turn (cumulative), from 0 to 100 percent
